b.x: This is a teaching scenario, not a forecast and not an order. It does not teach looting, breaking in, or a weapon. While the phone still lives: 193 if there is fire or someone stuck in the elevator, 192 if the body has failed, 190 if the violence is now. This page does not dial.

The power fails on a Tuesday, in the afternoon. It is not the film. It is the grid. The traffic light dies in the same minute. The phone still has battery and, for a while, some tower. Then the tower ends. The card does not go through. The gas-station pump does not start. The elevator stops where it was. In the building, the roof tank still comes down for a few hours, if nobody empties it for nothing. A closed refrigerator holds little: about four hours. A full freezer, about a day, if the door does not open all the time. A gas stove still works, if there is a cylinder and a match. An electric stove becomes weight. The bus disappears because the system and the pump's fuel stopped. Whoever is on the street walks back. Whoever is on a high floor takes the stairs.

The same hall. The same family on both sides: husband, wife, two children. The unprepared house buys groceries every other day. The gas cylinder is near the end. There is no stored water. The money is in the bank. The child's medicine lasts a few days. The prepared house is not a bunker. It is the house of this site. Stored water. Food the family already eats, enough for the week. A spare cylinder. One flashlight, not an altar of candles. A battery radio. Cash. Paper with the meeting point. The real medicine. Soap. The three-day bag is by the door. They do not leave on the first rumor.

In the first hour the unprepared house looks for a candle, opens the refrigerator several times, and goes down to see the street. The message does not send. The child is afraid of the dark. The prepared house closes the refrigerator, fills whatever still fits while the tap runs, checks the gas, turns on one light, and counts the four people. They agree on the water and the bathroom. They do not announce the stock in the hall. In the city, traffic locks because the signal died. The small market still serves, if the owner stayed. The line takes the water, the bread, and the battery. The cash machine is mute. At night the street is darker than usual. The danger of this night is not hunger. It is the fall on the stairs, the candle near the curtain, and the rumor.
The second and the third day

On the second day the unprepared house eats what thawed. If the meat stayed out, the smell starts. The building's water fails on the high floor. Yesterday's long shower was the last easy one. The phone is almost dead. The prepared house eats the usual plate, in a normal portion, not in a fear banquet. The water is measured: drinking and cooking first. One piece of news comes from the radio, not from the hall. The children have one small task and a bedtime. Neighbors knock. They ask for a candle, water, a phone charge. The house without stock has nothing to give. The house with stock gives a glass and a sentence, and does not open the pantry. On the third day the unprepared house's rice depends on the gas that is ending. The big market, if someone walks there, is no longer supply. It is a crowd, a shelf empty of water, and a rumor that the other neighborhood still has some. The prepared house does not go. On that day the market does not save. It spreads.
From the fourth to the seventh day

On the fourth and fifth day the unprepared house enters the trade. One neighbor has gas, another has rice, nobody has enough water. The hall argues about the roof tank. People who never spoke now measure someone else's door. Some families walk to a relative's house and do not come back the same day. The prepared house stays dull. The water still lasts if they measured from Tuesday. If they did not measure, it tightens too: prepared is not infinite. They know which day the water ends. They do not light the window. They do not count the stock aloud. On the sixth and seventh, if the power has not returned, the city smells of garbage. The hospital still runs on a generator, with a line, and it is not a market. The dirty-hand disease arrives before the film's hunger. The unprepared house is thirsty, the children are crying, and the couple is fighting over a decision that was not made on Tuesday. The prepared house is tired and whole. They ate. They drank on a count. If the water ends on the seventh day, they do not enter the crowd. They treat what they can, or they walk early, the four together, to the point on the paper, with the bag that looks like travel. Not at dawn in the dark. Not one alone.

It does not teach breaking into a market. It does not teach closing the street. It does not turn the neighbor into an enemy. A glass of water for whoever knocks is not opening the pantry. The difference between the two houses was not courage on the fifth day. It was water, food the mouth already accepts, gas, one light, paper, soap, and a closed mouth, decided before Tuesday. The unprepared family suffers the week. The prepared family crosses it tired. Neither becomes a film. One lives worse. The other still has a choice.
